results.title: Swedish government wants to ease ethics review requirements
results.content: # Swedish government wants to ease ethics review requirements. Swedish government wants to ease ethics review requirements. > This does not apply to medical research but to the social sciences and the humanities, says Lotta Edholm (L), Minister for Upper Secondary Education, Higher Education and Research. One example she points to is that political scientists need ethics approval to conduct research on the opinions of parliamentarians, even though those opinions are openly expressed in newspaper articles, on social media and in parliament. Whether participants in a study have provided informed consent; whether the data included in the research is already widely disseminated; and whether the data comes from judgments or government decisions. The government also wants to remove the mandatory requirement for the Ethics Review Board to file a complaint in the event of any reasonable suspicion of a crime. This requirement, says Lotta Edholm, has exposed researchers to unnecessary pressure and has created unnecessary work within the legal system.

results.title: Experiences of Ethical Review: Perspectives of Swedish ...
results.content: Some of the participants said that a much too strong focus on ethical review and how to fill in the ethics application takes time away from discussion on other important topics in research ethics – not least when it comes to teaching research ethics to PhD students. Another participant – also coming from the humanities – stressed that the requirement of ethical review had led to a much broader ethical discussion within their field of research. Some participants provided examples of research that might be difficult to perform because of ethical review. As already noted, the participants said that the ethical review system is overly restrictive as it requires ethical approval for research on publicly available sensitive personal data. In this article, we have presented findings from 7 semi-structured group interviews with researchers in social sciences and the humanities concerning their experiences and perceptions of ethical review in Sweden.
